Quick notes up front:
- Redwood supports SAML 2.0 (SP-initiated & IdP-initiated) and OIDC (authorization code + PKCE).

- RBAC: role model + resource-scoped roles, delegated admin, and audit trails.

We can provide deployment-specific caveats in the matrix (notably network access for Private and org-level SCIM integration options for Dedicated). We'll have a first draft by EOD Tuesday PST and can set a 30-min deep-dive after that. What time zone is best for you on Wednesday?

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: RFI: Identity & Access Management (SAML/OIDC, SCIM, RBAC) - technical responses and artifacts

Arjun —

Please find our initial responses below (summary) and attached artifacts. I've also attached our SAML XML metadata and an excerpted SCIM quickref. I'll highlight where behavior differs by deployment mode. Full matrix attached as RFI_IAM_matrix_v1.2.xlsx.

1) SAML / OIDC
- SAML 2.0: Supported (SP-initiated and IdP-initiated). We support SHA-256 signatures and HTTP-POST/Redirect bindings. Exchanges: support IdP metadata URL or direct XML upload; our console accepts metadata upload for hosted and Dedicated; for Private deployments we provide a metadata XML and can coordinate manual exchange.
- NameID & attributes: configurable NameID formats (email, persistent); attribute mapping in the admin console (map SAML attributes to user.email, user.displayName, groups).
- OIDC: Authorization Code flow + PKCE supported. We expose /authorize and /token endpoints and support standard claims (sub, name, email, email_verified). Token lifetimes configurable per org (default access_token: 1h, refresh_token: 30d with refresh reuse).

2) SCIM provisioning
- SCIM 2.0: Full support for Users and Groups endpoints (/scim/v2/Users, /scim/v2/Groups). Methods: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE. PATCH supports add/replace/remove per RFC 7644.
- Auth & secrets: Bearer tokens (admin token) for hosted; for Dedicated we support scoped API keys and optional mTLS for Private.
- Delta sync: incremental filters via "startIndex" and support for list pagination and filtering by externalId.
- Group push & membership: We support group push, nested groups (up to one level), and membership sync.
- Attribute extensibility: Custom attribute mapping available; we accept enterprise extensions using urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User for manager/title fields.
- Rate limits: 120 requests/min org-level by default; can be adjusted for Dedicated contracts.

3) RBAC & admin controls
- Role model: system roles (Organization Owner, Admin, Billing Admin, App Editor, Viewer) + resource-scoped roles for model endpoints and routes.
- Fine-grained policies: route-level allow/deny by role, and optional policy bindings to group attributes synchronized via SCIM.
- Delegated admin: Support for multi-tenant org admins and ability to create sub-admin roles.
- MFA & session controls: We enforce session timeouts and support enforced SSO (disable password auth for org). MFA integrations via IdP (asserted in SAML) or our native TOTP for hosted accounts.
- Audit logging: Admin actions, SSO events, and SCIM provisioning events are logged. Standard retention: 13 months for hosted; configurable for Dedicated and Private (can be exported to customer SIEM via syslog/forwarder).

4) Deployment-specific caveats
- Hosted (Redwood API): SCIM endpoints are publicly reachable via token bearer auth. SAML metadata upload via Console.
- Dedicated: Same features; network egress/internal IP allowlist may be required for SCIM push; higher rate limits available under contract.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): We provide metadata and SCIM endpoint documentation for local deployment. For air-gapped installs, SCIM provisioning can be proxied through customer network; SAML exchange typically manual.

Attachments included: RFI_IAM_matrix_v1.2.xlsx, redwood_saml_metadata.xml, scim_api_quickref.pdf

If you want, I can paste the SAML endpoints and example assertions in the call.

- Mina Haddad
Security Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference

Mina —

Thanks, this is very helpful. A couple follow-ups: 1) Do you support Signed Assertions encrypted with AES-256? 2) For SCIM, do you return a 429 with Retry-After or a 503 backoff? 3) Can group membership be filtered based on attribute (we want to only sync groups prefixed with FC-)?

Also — please call out whether audit logs include the original SAML NameID in events (we need an audit trail to map sessions to identities).

Best,
Arjun

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Arjun Mehta <arjun.mehta@fortunecorp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-03T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: RFI: Identity & Access Management (SAML/OIDC, SCIM, RBAC) - clarifications

Arjun —

Responses inline: 1) Encryption: We support encrypted assertions using AES-256 (XML Encryption) for hosted and Dedicated; for Private we can enable it in the customer config. 2) Rate limiting behavior: SCIM endpoints return 429 with a Retry-After header. For burst scenarios we also respond 503 when backend degraded; we include a Retry-After in both cases. 3) Group filtering: Yes — we support prefix/suffix filtering rules in the SCIM connector (you can supply a regex or prefix like "FC-" to limit synced groups).

Audit logs: We record the SAML NameID and the mapped internal user ID in session logs for hosted and Dedicated. For Private deployments you can configure whether NameID is persisted or redacted; we recommend persisting for 90 days to support investigations.

Next steps: Laura — can we schedule a 30-min technical call tomorrow (Wed 03/04) to walk the RFI matrix and exchange SAML metadata endpoints? I'm available 10:00-13:00 PT.

Thanks,
Mina
